result.title: Towards an Optimal Control Foundation of Early Exits - Turnpikes and ResNets
result.summary: The feed-forward propagation through neural networks is crucial for training and inference. To trade off efficiency and accuracy, it has been proposed to consider intermediate outputs of hidden states as data-dependent regularization during training and, ultimately, as early-exits during inference. In this work, we analyze the joint optimization of loss functions computed for the output layer and intermediate layers using optimal control theory. We prove that ResNets trained in this joint fashion exhibit the so-called turnpike phenomenon, this implies that the number of layers required to reach a prescribed loss level is bounded from above independently of the overall network depth. This induces a similarity property across the internal representations of early-exiting networks of varying depths. We connect the turnpike to the overthinking phenomenon, and provide theoretical insights into the success of early-exit criteria derived from softmax probabilities, specifically entropy and max-probability. In a range of experiments, we demonstrate the existence and effect of turnpikes and the resulting similarity in the early-exit performance for ResNets of varying depths.

AI.brief_summary: 论文用最优控制理论分析对输出层与中间层损失进行联合优化的 ResNet，证明其呈现 turnpike 现象，即达到指定损失所需层数存在与总深度无关的上界，并由此导出不同深度网络内部表示的相似性；还将该现象与 overthinking 联系，解释基于 softmax 熵和最大概率的早退准则，并用实验验证。
AI.relevance_reason: 其关于早退深度、停止准则和跨深度内部表示相似性的理论，可能为 LVR 的 STOP 决策、动态计算及 latent 相似性受深度影响等问题提供可供核查的线索；但研究对象并非视觉或多模态推理，迁移需进一步确认。
